324.h: Skyline University Nigeria (SUN) is a private university that received Federal Government approval in May 2018. It was the first private university in Kano and the second in north-western Nigeria. Since opening it has grown to five schools, each with its own departments.
324.a: The School of Science and Information Technology offers computer science, data science, cyber security, software engineering, artificial intelligence, biochemistry, geology and microbiology. The School of Arts, Management and Social Sciences covers mass communication, entrepreneurship, economics, business administration, accounting, international relations, and Islamic economics and finance. The School of Basic Medical Sciences offers physiotherapy, nursing, basic medical science and public health, and the School of Legal Studies offers the LL.B. law degree. A School of Postgraduate Studies runs master's programmes, including an MBA and degrees in economics, forensic accounting, computer science and diplomatic studies.
324.c: It is located in Kano, the capital of Kano State.

347.h: Western Delta University (WDU) is a private university established in 2007 by a group of Urhobo scholars through the Urhobo Advancement Foundation. They saw the need for a privately funded university in the wetlands of Delta State. The National Universities Commission granted it a provisional licence.
347.a: WDU uses a collegiate system, with colleges of Natural and Applied Sciences, Social and Management Sciences, Applied Health Sciences, Law, Computing and Postgraduate Studies. Courses include biochemistry, microbiology and biotechnology, and industrial chemistry. Applicants come through JAMB's UTME or by direct entry with a diploma, an NCE or two A-level passes. They need five O-level credits, including English Language and Mathematics, at no more than two sittings.
347.c: It is located at Unoghovo-Oghara, Delta State.

224.h: Arthur Jarvis University (AJU) is a private university founded in 2016. It was the first private university in Cross River State.
224.a: The Faculty of Natural and Applied Sciences covers the biological, chemical and earth sciences (including geology and applied geophysics), physics, and a computing group with computer science, cyber security, software engineering, data science and artificial intelligence. The Faculty of Humanities, Management and Social Sciences offers accounting, banking and finance, business administration, entrepreneurship, criminology and security studies, marketing, economics, mass communication, political science, public administration, hospitality and tourism, and sociology with peace and conflict resolution.
224.c: It is located in Akpabuyo, near Calabar, the capital of Cross River State.

270.h: Federal University, Otuoke (FUOtuoke) is one of the nine federal universities established in February 2011 under President Goodluck Jonathan, whose home town is Otuoke. It started with 282 pioneer students. The university has taken a firm line on misconduct: it expelled 12 students in March 2019 and 29 more in December 2019 for cultism and examination malpractice.
270.a: The university has six faculties and offers undergraduate degrees and postgraduate diplomas, master's degrees and doctorates. Its central library opened with the university, and together with the faculty libraries and the Bruce Powell E-Library it seats about 1,500 readers.
270.c: It is in Otuoke, a town in the Ogbia local government area of Bayelsa State, in the oil-producing Niger Delta.

269.h: Federal University, Lokoja (FUL) was established by the Federal Government in February 2011, as one of nine new federal universities created to meet demand for university places. Its library opened the same year, with Dr Adekunle Kareem Sanusi as the pioneer university librarian.
269.a: The university has faculties of Sciences, Arts, Social Sciences, Management Sciences and Education, and a College of Health Sciences. It has an agreement with the Institute of Sales and Marketing Management of Nigeria to enrol students in a diploma in sales and marketing management, and the Independent Corrupt Practices Commission runs an anti-corruption unit on campus.
269.c: It has two campuses in Lokoja, the capital of Kogi State: the permanent campus at Felele and another at Adankolo. Lokoja lies where the Niger and Benue rivers meet.

325.h: Sokoto State University (SSU) is a public university owned by the Sokoto State Government. Governor Aliyu Wamakko set up an implementation committee in 2008 to plan its facilities and seek Federal Government approval, which came in 2009. A key motive was access: under the federal character principle, the state's own indigenes held relatively few places at the federal Usmanu Danfodiyo University in the same city.
325.a: The committee also created a School of Developmental Studies to run a one-year pre-degree programme that prepares students for entry to the university. The university's stated aims include giving people from Sokoto State access to higher education for self-reliance.
325.c: It is located in Sokoto, the capital of Sokoto State in north-western Nigeria.

265.h: Federal University, Gashua (FUGashua) was established under President Goodluck Jonathan, as part of a programme of twelve new federal universities across the six geopolitical zones. Professor Shehu Abdul Rahman was appointed its pioneer vice-chancellor on 18 February 2013. The university admitted its first 240 students in June 2015, and had matriculated 990 students by February 2018. Its library was set up in 2013.
265.a: The university offers undergraduate programmes and is developing its range of courses under a five-year development plan.
265.c: It is located in Gashua, Yobe State, in north-eastern Nigeria.

313.h: Pan-Atlantic University (PAU) is a private, non-profit university that grew out of the Lagos Business School, founded in 1991 to provide executive education and management training. The Federal Government approved the university in 2002, with the business school as its first school. Schools of Media and Communication and of Science and Technology were added later.
313.a: PAU is best known for business and management education through the Lagos Business School. It also offers media and communication, and science and technology. In 2011 it launched an online Virtual Museum of Modern Nigerian Art with more than 400 works, and in 2019 it opened the Yemisi Shyllon Museum of Art, one of the largest private museums in Nigeria.
313.c: The university completed a campus at Ajah in 2003 and began building its main campus at Ibeju-Lekki, Lagos State, in 2010.
